answer: The Original Costa Route: Both Coasts is a 10-day Costa Rica itinerary, a deviation from the original from James Wild & Co. built only on Cayuga Collection hotels: three nights at Aguas Claras on the Caribbean, three at Senda Monteverde in the cloud forest and three at Arenas del Mar on the Pacific, with a surf day on each coast and a day at Dominical. You travel by private driver from San José.
daytitle: The Original Costa Route: Both Coasts

days.title: San José to the Caribbean
days.line: Private driver over the mountains · ~4 hr
days.body: Met at San José airport and driven down through the rainforest to the Caribbean coast. By evening you're at Aguas Claras near Puerto Viejo, where the colour, the music and the food are a different country from the Pacific.
days.imgAlt: The Caribbean coast and reef near Playa Chiquita from the air

days.title: The reef at Playa Chiquita
days.body: At low tide the reef makes clear pools you can swim in from the beach. Afternoon on a bicycle into Puerto Viejo, or a ride along the sand.
days.img: PHOTO · THE REEF AT PLAYA CHIQUITA
days.imgAlt: A swimmer in a clear tide pool on the reef at Playa Chiquita, near Aguas Claras

days.title: The Caribbean surf day
days.line: A board waiting on the other coast
days.body: A board sized for you and a local surf guide who knows the Caribbean side's reef breaks and when to leave them alone. Or the beach on horseback.
days.imgAlt: A rider galloping a horse along a Caribbean beach

days.title: Across the country
days.line: Caribbean to the cloud forest · a long day
days.body: The longest day: across the country from the Caribbean to Monteverde by private driver, about 6.5 hours with a lunch stop [we may suggest a small charter flight to shorten it; confirm]. You arrive at Senda for the evening.
days.move: Private driver · ~6.5 hr, or a charter flight [confirm]
days.imgAlt: A guest with coffee on a balcony in the cloud forest at Senda Monteverde

days.title: The Aguti trails
days.line: Walk as far as your legs go
days.body: Senda guests walk the neighbouring Aguti Wildlife Reserve as often as they like. Go early with a naturalist, and take the night walk after dark when the frogs come out.
days.imgAlt: Birders looking up at a giant buttressed tree at Senda Monteverde

days.title: Quetzal at dawn
days.line: A birding guide and a telescope
days.body: Out at first light for the quetzal, then a free afternoon in the hot pools in the forest.
days.imgAlt: A resplendent quetzal in flight among cloud-forest trees at Senda Monteverde

days.title: Down to the Pacific
days.line: Private driver to Manuel Antonio · ~4 hr
days.body: Down from the mountains to the second ocean. By afternoon you're at Arenas del Mar, where the rainforest runs straight onto two beaches.
days.imgAlt: A rainforest headland meeting a turquoise beach at Manuel Antonio, from the air

days.title: Manuel Antonio
days.line: The park with a naturalist, then the beach
days.body: Into Manuel Antonio National Park early with a naturalist [park days and hours to confirm]. The afternoon is the beach's.
days.imgAlt: A long curved beach backed by rainforest, seen from the hillside at Arenas del Mar

days.title: The founder's day
days.line: Dominical, and a board if you want one
days.body: South along the coast to Dominical, about 45 minutes, where James sat for his 1995 photo. Lunch by the beach. Surfers take the board that's waiting: Dominical if it's happening, a secret spot or a side trip down the coast if it isn't.
days.imgAlt: Polaroid of James relaxing on a beach in a patterned shirt, Dominical, Costa Rica, 1995

days.title: Home
days.line: Out through San José or Quepos
days.body: A short flight from Quepos to San José, or the drive back, about 3 hours [confirm], and the flight home. If the swell is running at Pavones, James will tell you before you leave: cancel the flight and head south.
days.imgAlt: Footprints in the sand on a beach looking out to small islands at Arenas del Mar

founder.title: Surf travel since 1992. Cayuga since 1994.
founder.p1: James has pioneered surf travel in Costa Rica since 1992, when the boards rode on the roof and the coast road was mostly a rumour. He has followed Hans Pfister, Cayuga's co-founder, since 1994, from his early days selling these lodges.
founder.p2: This is the coast-to-coast version: the Caribbean first, for colour and a reef you can swim from the beach, then the cloud forest, then the Pacific and a day at Dominical, where his 1995 photo was taken. A board waits on both coasts.

faqs: Can you see both coasts of Costa Rica in 10 days?
Yes. Three nights on the Caribbean, three in the cloud forest and three on the Pacific is the right pace. The one long day is crossing the country, which a short charter flight can shorten.
What's the difference between Costa Rica's Caribbean and Pacific coasts?

The Caribbean side around Puerto Viejo is greener, wetter and Afro-Caribbean in its food and music; the Pacific is drier in the dry season, with bigger resort towns and national parks like Manuel Antonio. This route gives you both.
Which Cayuga hotels does this route use?
Aguas Claras on the Caribbean, Senda Monteverde in the cloud forest and Arenas del Mar at Manuel Antonio, all part of the Cayuga Collection.
When is the best time to visit both coasts?
The coasts keep different weather. February to April and September to October are often good on both sides; we check the season for your dates [confirm].
Can I surf on both coasts?
Yes. A board waits on each coast with a local surf guide: the Caribbean side's reef breaks on Day 3, and Dominical if it's happening, or a secret spot if it isn't, on Day 9.

Pavones, near the Panama border, is one of the longest left-hand waves anywhere, and it only really works on the right swell. If it's running when you're due to leave, James will let you know. Cancel your flight, head south, and we'll rebook you home.
Are there offers on this route?

Often. In 2026 Aguas Claras has stay 4 nights, pay 3 (not in October) if you add a night, Senda Monteverde has stay 3 nights, pay 2, and booking Senda and Arenas del Mar together brings a free room upgrade, subject to availability.
How much does The Original Costa Route: Both Coasts cost?

From $2,510 per person in the green season (May to November) and from $3,575 in the dry season (December to April), two sharing, plus 7% Florida sales tax. That covers the hotels as listed, with hotel taxes, and the private drivers. The route is booked subject to lodge availability and isn't offered over Christmas and New Year.

lodges_title: Three Cayuga hotels, coast to coast

lodges.name: Aguas Claras
lodges.body: Nine bungalows and six suites near Puerto Viejo, each one a living art installation in the jungle, Cayuga says. The Caribbean side of Costa Rica: colour, music, food and a reef you can swim from the beach.
rows: Private driver from San José, ~4 hr

lodges.name: Senda Monteverde
lodges.body: A cloud-forest hotel beside the Aguti Wildlife Reserve, with unlimited hiking for guests, hot pools in the trees and a restaurant that lights up at dusk. Cayuga calls it the hotel for the down-to-earth explorer.
rows: Monteverde, beside the Aguti Wildlife Reserve
Private driver from the Caribbean, ~6.5 hr, or a charter flight [confirm]

lodges.name: Arenas del Mar
lodges.body: The only luxury resort in Manuel Antonio right on the beach, Cayuga says: two pools, two beaches and two restaurants on 11 acres of rainforest. Easy for families and first-timers.
